canon_capabilities: FTL travel inside a subspace bubble that distorts local spacetime
Galaxy class: warp 9.6 for a few hours, past the red line above 9.3, 9.8 at extreme risk (Encounter at Farpoint)
slow reverse impulse to warp 9 in 0.3 ms (The Last Outpost)
canon_limits: warp 10 is unattainable, infinite on the 24th-century scale (VOY Threshold)
2.7 million ly would take 300+ years at maximum warp (Where No One Has Gone Before)
nacelle imbalance can open a wormhole (TMP)
physics_basis: General relativity allows warp metrics (Alcubierre): space contracts ahead of a bubble and expands behind, and the interior falls freely, so a 0.3 ms jump to warp is survivable; dampers (M-011) take the field's formation and collapse. GR alone needs negative energy, puts a superluminal bubble's front beyond the ship's control (Krasnikov) and lets FTL make time loops (Everett). P1 supplies the geometry; P2 carries control across the wall and keeps FTL causal. On-screen speeds conflict; the warp factor is read as a field grade, capped by the M33 figure.
engineering_gap: Coils that turn antimatter power into a stable, steerable bubble around a 640 m hull; we have the metric on paper and no way to source it.

canon_capabilities: sublight propulsion for maneuvering and in-system travel
fusion impulse reactors (The Battle; Contagion displays)

canon_limits: sublight only

physics_basis: Fusion rockets are real physics, but a bare one can't match canon: a perfect D-T rocket must start about 19 times heavier than it ends to reach the manuals' 0.25 c, yet canon ships make repeated full-impulse runs. The augmentation is P1: driver coils (on screen later; their role is a Technical Manual reading) lower the hull's effective inertia through subspace, the coupling dampers use, so fusion gives power and trim thrust. The motion is real, so relativity applies and ship clocks lag.
engineering_gap: Steady compact fusion, and driver coils that cut a 5-million-tonne hull's effective inertia many-fold.

failure_modes: Driver-coil loss leaves only the rocket: gentle maneuvers, no big speed changes
Driver field lost at speed: momentum is conserved as inertia returns, so the ship brakes hard onto the dampers
Reactor overload: a ship-killing fusion blast

canon_capabilities: deuterium and antideuterium react in a dilithium matrix, giving plasma for warp and ship power
dilithium regulates the reaction; recrystallized in place by the 2360s (Time Squared)
the core can be ejected (TOS; later TNG)
canon_limits: antimatter is held only by magnetic containment; collapse destroys the ship in minutes (11001001)
dilithium slowly decrystallizes; crude or drained crystals give erratic power (TOS)
dilithium is rare and must be mined
physics_basis: Annihilation is real: matter meeting antimatter releases its whole rest energy, hundreds of times fusion's per kilogram, and antihydrogen has been held in magnetic traps. But proton-antiproton annihilation happens on contact and emits pions, gamma rays and neutrinos, so it can't be throttled and much of it escapes as radiation. P3 is that missing piece: dilithium couples to subspace and regulates the reaction into usable plasma without being consumed; its slow decrystallization is read as lattice fatigue. Storage is real magnetic trapping, scaled up.
engineering_gap: Antimatter by the tonne (we have made nanograms), bulk magnetic storage, and a dilithium supply.

Dilithium fracture: output sags or surges; recrystallize, replace, or go to impulse

canon_capabilities: breaks the subject into a particle stream, buffers it, sends it across subspace and reassembles it (Datalore)
about 40,000 km range (later canon); site-to-site and intraship (Symbiosis, 11001001)

canon_limits: needs a lock; not through raised shields

physics_basis: Quantum teleportation moves a state by measurement plus a classical message, destroying the original; no-cloning forbids copies and the uncertainty principle forbids exact readout. Canon's 'matter to energy' is read as disassembly into a particle stream (Datalore), since converting a person to energy would release about 1500 Mt. Carrying stream and full state through subspace and rebuilding within biological tolerance is P4, the Heisenberg compensators its sealed part. Light crosses 40,000 km in under a second, so P2 isn't needed.
engineering_gap: Scanning and buffering some 7e27 atoms in seconds over 40,000 km; the compensators stay a black box.

canon_capabilities: transporter-type conversion makes food and objects from replicator stores (Lonely Among Us)

physics_basis: Making matter from energy is real physics but absurd: 1 kg takes 9e16 J. So canon's 'matter-energy conversion' is read as rearrangement: stored and recycled feedstock is streamed and rebuilt to a stored pattern by the transporter's reassembly (P4) at molecular, not quantum, resolution (a Technical Manual distinction). Molecular assembly breaks no physical law; its cost is bond energy and heat. The coarser resolution explains taste quirks, no living things, and compounds whose action depends on finer structure.
engineering_gap: Placing some 1e25 atoms in seconds at molecular accuracy, with heat handling to match.

canon_capabilities: deflect most matter and concentrated energy, phasers and torpedoes included
strength read as a percentage; can be extended over another ship (TOS Mudd's Women)
held, weakened, through a solar flare (Symbiosis)
canon_limits: sustained or heavy fire wears them down until they fail

physics_basis: Real physics shields against charged particles: a 1 tesla field curls a 30 MeV proton within about a metre, the idea behind proposed active shielding for crewed spacecraft. But no practical field stops fast neutral matter, and light passes through static fields unaffected. Gravity bends everything, but bending a beam 0.1 rad at 10 m would take the gravity of 3.4e26 kg. So a shield is P1: a shaped layer of spacetime geometry around the hull that deflects whatever crosses it. Absorbed energy loads the generators, so fire wears it down, and the layer scatters the transporter's subspace stream.
engineering_gap: Generators that hold a closed geometry layer around the whole hull and take megaton-class hits without burning out.

canon_limits: overdriving it can damage the ship's power systems (TOS The Paradise Syndrome)

physics_basis: Interstellar space holds roughly one atom per cubic centimetre, plus dust. Met at 0.25 c, each hydrogen atom arrives as a 31 MeV proton and a microgram grain carries about 3 MJ, so a ship at high impulse needs a sweeper. Charged particles can be swept by real magnetic and electric fields, and neutral gas ionized first; dust and debris need P1, the shaped geometry of M-006 projected forward. At warp the dish also keeps matter from piling into the bubble wall (M-001).
engineering_gap: A forward field wide and strong enough to clear a 473 m by 133 m path at relativistic speed for years without eroding the dish.

canon_capabilities: hand and ship phasers set from stun through kill to disintegration
heat rock, cut walls and stone

canon_limits: hand phasers can overload and explode, with a rising whine first (TOS)
some materials and beings are unaffected; Armus fed on phaser fire (Skin of Evil)
point-blank stun to a vital organ can kill (Star Trek VI)
ship phasers draw on main power (TMP)
physics_basis: Stun, heating and cutting are real directed-energy physics: a laser-guided plasma channel can carry a disabling current (electrolaser), and focused beams heat and cut. The gaps are beam control and storage: vaporizing a 70 kg body takes about 1.8e8 J, some 200 kg of today's batteries. Disintegration is the one effect real physics plus P1-P4 can't give: that energy released in the target would hit the room like 42 kg of TNT, yet canon shows a quiet glow and nothing left. It is flagged, not explained. Armus is a canon unknown.
engineering_gap: Cells holding a 200 kg battery's energy in a hand unit, and beams that put it at a chosen depth without blooming.

canon_capabilities: warp-capable matter-antimatter weapon with an antimatter detonation chamber
launchers fire salvos of up to five (The Arsenal of Freedom)

physics_basis: The warhead is real physics: matter and antimatter held apart, then mixed at detonation, releasing their full rest energy. The TNG Technical Manual's 1.5 kg of antideuterium gives the 64 Mt computed below. In vacuum there is no blast wave: the energy leaves as gamma rays, pions and their decay products and does damage by radiation and surface heating, falling off with the square of distance. Holding antimatter in a trap is engineering; flying at warp needs P1, a small sustainer field.
engineering_gap: Kilogram-scale antimatter traps that survive launch, maneuvering and enemy fire, and a warp sustainer that fits a torpedo casing.

tech: sensors (ship and tricorder, EM and subspace)
canon_capabilities: multi-spectral sensors, passive and active, short and long range (Encounter at Farpoint)
a deep sensor probe clears space of vessels to three light years (Skin of Evil)

physics_basis: The near channel is real physics: radar, lidar, spectroscopy and imaging, bound by light speed, diffraction and what penetrates matter. A 0.2 m aperture resolves a person from orbit, but a 10 m aperture resolves only about 66 km at a light-hour and an EM sweep to 3 ly returns in 6 years. Canon's prompt long-range results therefore need P2: subspace pulses read the subspace imprint of mass and energy (P1's coupling) faster than light, at coarser resolution. Masking by matter and radiation is the EM channel's real limit.
engineering_gap: Subspace emitters and receivers sensitive enough to find ships light years off, fused with EM returns in real time.

canon_capabilities: deck gravity plating; areas can be low or variable gravity (Encounter at Farpoint gym; shuttlebays)
dampers absorb the ship's accelerations and the shock of hits (later canon)
canon_limits: without dampers, accelerations and warp jumps would kill the crew (VOY Tattoo)

an automatic bypass guards against disabled dampers (Cost of Living)
physics_basis: Einstein's equivalence principle makes these one problem: uniform gravity and acceleration are locally indistinguishable, and a body in free fall feels nothing. A damper is a field that makes the crew fall with the ship as it accelerates; deck gravity is a steady field of the same kind. Real physics makes neither without huge mass (1 g at 10 m needs 1.5e13 kg) or rotation, so both are P1. Reaching 0.25 c in a minute is about 1.3e5 g, so the damper must cancel all but about eight millionths, and any lag is a jolt. The field must be even across a body, or tides pull at it.
engineering_gap: Field control fast and even enough to track 1e5 g to parts per million, deck by deck, with failover.

physics_basis: Light and sound already hold small things (optical tweezers, acoustic levitation), but only by pushing; holding a shuttle with light would take petawatts and still could not pull. The consistent reading of canon's graviton beam is P1: a narrow, shaped geometry gradient the target falls along. Momentum is still conserved, as The Naked Now shows, where pushing on the Tsiolkovsky moved the Enterprise. The emitting ship takes the reaction, so heavy loads drag it and call on its engines, and uneven pull across the target stresses it.
engineering_gap: Focusing a geometry gradient into a steerable beam over kilometres and holding it on a moving target.

physics_basis: Radio is real physics: light speed, inverse-square spreading, and capacity set by bandwidth and signal-to-noise (Shannon-Hartley). Relativity makes any FTL signal a possible message into the past (tachyonic antitelephone), so FTL needs P2, whose no-paradox clause amounts to a preferred causal frame. Canon's speeds conflict: the M33 figure gives about 52,000 c, under which a live call would fail beyond about 50 AU, yet canon shows live calls across light years. Most consistent reading: P2 fixes no one speed; it rises with transmitter power and relays, and M33 is a lone ship's floor.
engineering_gap: Transmitters and a relay network strong enough to carry live speech across light years.

Solid objects that push back are force fields under P1, a weak local cousin of the tractor beam; real diamagnetic levitation of a body would need the field-gradient product below throughout the room. Food, water and props are replicated (P4) and persist outside. Field-held objects exist only within the emitters' reach and vanish at the door; canon's slow fades are read as residual fields near the exit. Safeties cap the force any field delivers.

canon_capabilities: hand and ship phasers set from stun through kill to disintegration
heat rock, cut walls and stone
ship phasers fire beams or bursts, stun a surface from orbit, and can transfer power as a beam (TOS; Encounter at Farpoint)
canon_limits: hand phasers can overload and explode, with a rising whine first (TOS)

physics_basis: Stun, heating and cutting are real directed-energy physics: a laser-guided plasma channel can carry a disabling current (electrolaser), and focused beams heat and cut. Disintegration can't be heat: gasifying a 70 kg body takes about 1.8e8 J and fills a cabin with over 100 m3 of steam. It is P5. The beam drives the target's matter into neutrinos and antineutrinos, the way core-collapse supernovae shed 99% of their energy. The target pays for its own disappearance, its full rest energy of 1,504 Mt, and that energy leaves through the ship and the planet almost untouched; the body's B-L of 1.9e28 leaves as surplus antineutrinos. Momentum forbids a beamed exhaust, since a one-sided burst would carry 2.1e10 kg m/s, so the emission is symmetric. The glow is the fraction that leaks into light. Every disintegration is a neutrino flash any sensor in the system can read. Overload is the cell dumping its store the ordinary way. Armus is a canon unknown.
engineering_gap: Cells holding cabin-wrecking energy in a hand unit, and the focusing and conditioning train that drives P5 and holds its output in a safe state: a soft spectrum near 10 MeV, where a bystander takes a few CT scans' worth instead of a lethal dose; a light leak below 1e-12; and conversion that stops the instant the beam leaves the target.
